newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Fedesarrollo head said tapped for Colombia cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Fedesarrollo head said tapped for Colombia cenbank.

text.p: Mauricio Cardenas, head of Colombia's prestigious economic think-tank Fedesarrollo, will fill a vacancy on the policy-making board of directors of Colombia's central bank, Bogota's El Espectador newspaper said.

Cardenas, an economist educated at the University of California at Berkeley who served as Development Minister under former president Cesar Gaviria, could not be reached for immediate comment on the report.

As director of Fedesarrollo, an independent think-tank, Cardenas has voiced criticism of some of the economic measures adopted by the embattled government of President Ernesto Samper. His appointment would be read as an effort by Samper to appoint independent economists to the central bank.

If news of his appointment is confirmed, Cardenas would be the fourth person on the central bank's seven-member board of directors who owes his post to Samper. Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo is one of the seven co-directors of the bank, which operates independently of the central government and is solely responsible for monetary policy.

The government announced earlier this week that Samper had appointed Luis Bernardo Florez, outgoing chief of the state oil company Ecopetrol, to fill another vacancy on the board of the Banco de la Republica, as the central bank is officially known.
